events.name: Quadrantids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: A strong annual meteor shower with a short peak window. Best viewed from dark northern skies after midnight.

events.name: Wolf Moon
events.description: The first full Moon of the year. Bright moonlight can reduce meteor visibility.

events.name: New Moon
events.description: Dark skies around new Moon are ideal for deep-sky observing.

events.name: Snow Moon
events.description: A bright winter full Moon that rises near sunset.

events.name: New Moon
events.description: A low-glare night for observing galaxies, nebulae, and star clusters.

events.name: March Equinox
events.description: Day and night are nearly equal across much of Earth as the Sun crosses the celestial equator.

events.name: Lyrids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: The Lyrids can produce bright, fast meteors. Look toward Lyra after midnight.

events.name: Eta Aquariids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Dust from Halley's Comet creates this shower. It favors southern hemisphere observers.

events.name: June Solstice
events.description: The Sun reaches its northernmost apparent position, marking summer in the north and winter in the south.

events.name: Delta Aquariids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: A steady meteor shower best viewed from dark southern skies.

events.name: Perseids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: One of the most popular meteor showers of the year. The Perseids are known for bright meteors and occasional fireballs.

events.name: September Equinox
events.description: The Sun crosses the celestial equator, bringing autumn to the northern hemisphere.

events.name: Orionids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Another Halley's Comet shower, with swift meteors radiating from Orion.

events.name: Taurids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: The Taurids are slow and can produce bright fireballs over a long observing window.

events.name: Leonids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: The Leonids are famous for rare meteor storms, though most years are modest.

events.name: December Solstice
events.description: The Sun reaches its southernmost apparent position, marking winter in the north and summer in the south.

events.name: Geminids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: Often the strongest annual meteor shower, produced by debris from asteroid 3200 Phaethon.

events.name: Ursids Meteor Shower Peak
events.description: A smaller northern meteor shower active near the December solstice.
